DiagProMeta 0.1.0

    DiagProMeta

    Sensitivity Analysis for Publication Bias on the SROC Curve

    DiagProMeta is an R package for the likelihood-based sensitivity analysis for publication bias

    • on the summary receiver operating characteristic (SROC) curve and the area under the SROC curve (SAUC) in meta-analysis of diagnostic test accuracy (Zhou et al., 2023), and
    • on the time-dependent SROC curve and SAUC in meta-analysis of prognostic studies, where the time-dependent sensitivity and specificity are reconstructed from the published survival probabilities (Combescure et al., 2016).

    The repository is named srocsa, but the package name is DiagProMeta.

    Installation

    The development version can be installed from GitHub:

    # install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("kusuri26/srocsa")

    DiagProMeta requires R (>= 3.5) and imports lifecycle, mixmeta, and numDeriv.

    Example

    The IVD data (Safdar et al., 2005) contain the 2 x 2 tables (TP, FN, FP, TN) of 33 diagnostic studies.

    library(DiagProMeta)
data(IVD)

## sensitivity analysis for the marginal selection probabilities p = 1, 0.8, 0.6
fit <- srocsa.t(TP = TP, FN = FN, TN = TN, FP = FP, data = IVD, sa.p = c(1, 0.8, 0.6))
fit
    SAUC Estimates
-------------------------------------------
Marginal p    SAUC      SE   CI.low   CI.up
-------------------------------------------
p = 1        0.874   0.029    0.806   0.920
p = 0.8      0.871   0.030    0.800   0.919
p = 0.6      0.822   0.041    0.727   0.889

    (Only the SAUC table is shown. print() also shows the convergence of the optimizer and the parameter estimates with their standard errors.)

    ## tables of the SAUC and the parameter estimates
res <- summary(fit)
res$sauc
res$coef

## SROC curves and summary points for each p
plot(fit)

    p = 1 corresponds to no publication bias. A smaller p assumes that a smaller proportion of the studies is published, and the change of the SROC curve and SAUC shows the potential impact of publication bias.

    Methods

    Sensitivity analysis on the SROC curve (srocsa.t)

    Let y1iy_{1i} and y2iy_{2i} be the logit-transformed sensitivity and specificity of study ii, and v1iv_{1i} and v2iv_{2i} be their variances. The bivariate random-effects model (Reitsma et al., 2005) is

    (y1i,y2i)⊤∼N((μ1,μ2)⊤,diag(v1i,v2i)+Ω), (y_{1i}, y_{2i})^\top \sim N\left((\mu_1, \mu_2)^\top,\ \mathrm{diag}(v_{1i}, v_{2i}) + \Omega\right),

    where Ω\Omega has the between-study standard deviations τ1,τ2\tau_1, \tau_2 and correlation ρ\rho. The probability of publishing study ii is modeled by the selection function Φ(α+βti)\Phi(\alpha + \beta t_i) with

    ti=c1y1i+c2y2ic12v1i+c22v2i,c1,c2≥0,c12+c22=1. t_i = \frac{c_1 y_{1i} + c_2 y_{2i}}{\sqrt{c_1^2 v_{1i} + c_2^2 v_{2i}}}, \quad c_1, c_2 \ge 0, \quad c_1^2 + c_2^2 = 1.

    For a given marginal selection probability pp, α\alpha is determined such that the mean of the inverse of the marginal selection probabilities of the observed studies equals 1/p1/p. The model is fitted by the maximum likelihood method for each pp in sa.p. c12c_1^2 is estimated by default, or fixed by the argument c11.

    Sensitivity analysis on the time-dependent SROC curve (tsrocsa.lrt)

    At each time point, the time-dependent sensitivity and specificity, and their within-study variances and covariance, are reconstructed from the survival probabilities of the test-positive and test-negative groups (Combescure et al., 2016). The logit-transformed sensitivity, specificity, and the log hazard ratio (lnHR) are modeled by the trivariate random-effects model, combined with the selection function on the tt-statistic of lnHR.

    Three data frames are required:

    Argument Content
    data.os Survival probabilities of the two groups, one row for each study and each time point
    data.lnhr lnHR and its variance, one row for each study
    data.mct Survival probabilities at the median follow-up time, used to estimate the censoring distribution

    See ?tsrocsa.lrt for the details of each column.

    Functions

    Function Description
    srocsa.t() Sensitivity analysis for publication bias on the SROC curve and SAUC
    tsrocsa.lrt() Sensitivity analysis for publication bias on the time-dependent SROC curve and SAUC
    sroc() Bivariate random-effects model for the SROC curve without publication bias
    tsroc() Time-dependent SROC curve without publication bias
    sauc() SAUC and its confidence interval (delta method on the logit scale)
    print(), summary(), plot() Methods for the "srocsa" objects returned by srocsa.t(), tsroc(), and tsrocsa.lrt()

    Data

    Data Description
    IVD Meta-analysis of the diagnosis of intravascular device-related bloodstream infection (33 studies)
    CD64 Meta-analysis of neutrophil CD64 for the diagnosis of bacterial infection (27 studies)
    IVD_2, CD64_2 Logit-transformed sensitivity and specificity of IVD and CD64, with their variances

    Example data for the time-dependent analysis are not yet included in the package.

    References

    • Zhou Y, Huang A, Hattori S (2023). A likelihood-based sensitivity analysis for publication bias on the summary receiver operating characteristic in meta-analysis of diagnostic test accuracy. Statistics in Medicine, 42(6), 781–798. doi:10.1002/sim.9643
    • Combescure C, Daures JP, Foucher Y (2016). A literature-based approach to evaluate the predictive capacity of a marker using time-dependent summary receiver operating characteristics. Statistical Methods in Medical Research, 25(2), 674–685. doi:10.1177/0962280212464542
    • Reitsma JB, Glas AS, Rutjes AW, Scholten RJ, Bossuyt PM, Zwinderman AH (2005). Bivariate analysis of sensitivity and specificity produces informative summary measures in diagnostic reviews. Journal of Clinical Epidemiology, 58(10), 982–990. doi:10.1016/j.jclinepi.2005.02.022
    • Safdar N, Fine JP, Maki DG (2005). Meta-analysis: methods for diagnosing intravascular device-related bloodstream infection. Annals of Internal Medicine, 142(6), 451–466. doi:10.7326/0003-4819-142-6-200503150-00011
